# J3 — Pin a `RichTextCodec` contract (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for Data Center)

## Context / Problem

Rich-text encoding is one of the three real differences between Jira Cloud and Data Center: Cloud's REST v3
requires Atlassian Document Format (a nested JSON document; sending a plain string returns 400), while DC's
REST v2 carries descriptions and comment bodies as plain text / wiki markup. Today ADF is hardwired into the
Cloud path — `adapters/jira/adf.py` provides `fit_text_to_adf_limit`, `normalize_description`, `text_to_adf`
and `adf_to_text`, and `adapters/jira/backend.py`'s `map_fields_to_remote` reaches the encoder through the
module-level helper `_fit_description` (`backend.py:32-42`), which calls `outbound_fields._load_adf()` and
composes `normalize_description(fit_text_to_adf_limit(value))`. PR #120's answer was to copy that whole method
and change the single ADF line, which is the duplication this epic exists to prevent.

## Approach

Define a `RichTextCodec` Protocol in `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py` [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] and give
it **four** operations, not two. Two is not enough to preserve today's Cloud behavior, because the Cloud path
today has three distinct rich-text steps that are used in different combinations by different callers:

| operation | Cloud (`AdfCodec`) | Data Center (`WikiTextCodec`) |
|---|---|---|
| `fit_outbound(text: str) -> str` | `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit` (binary-searches the largest prefix whose **ADF serialization** fits 32000) | character truncation at `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` |
| `normalize_outbound(text: str) -> str` | `adf.normalize_description` (rejoins soft wraps so the send value equals what a later fetch decodes) | identity — wiki markup has no soft-wrap rejoin |
| `to_wire(text: str) -> Any` | `adf.text_to_adf` → an ADF `dict` | the `str` unchanged |
| `decode_inbound(body: Any) -> str` | `adf.adf_to_text` (`""` for `None`) | the `str` unchanged (`""` for `None`) |

**Why four and not two.** The two existing Cloud call paths genuinely differ, and collapsing them would change
behavior that J1's oracles pin:

- `backend.py:_fit_description` composes **both** steps: `normalize_description(fit_text_to_adf_limit(v))`, in
  that exact order (fit first, then normalize). Its docstring records why the order is load-bearing.
- the relocated `jira_family.sanitize_description`, as J2 [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] landed it, is injected
  with the **fit step only** — Cloud binds `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit` and nothing else.

If `fit_outbound` silently subsumed normalization, `sanitize_description` would start normalizing and Cloud's
observable behavior would change. If it omitted normalization while `_fit_description` was re-pointed at it,
the send path would stop normalizing and description diffs would stop converging. Keeping `fit_outbound` and
`normalize_outbound` as separate primitives lets each caller compose exactly what it composes today:
`_fit_description` becomes `codec.normalize_outbound(codec.fit_outbound(v))`, and `sanitize_description`'s
injected `fit` becomes `codec.fit_outbound`. Both are behavior-preserving for Cloud, which is what J1's pinned
oracles require.

`to_wire` and `decode_inbound` are separate from the fit steps because `fit_text_to_adf_limit` returns **text**,
not an ADF document — the text→ADF conversion happens later, at the transport (`acli.py` wraps the sanitized
description in `text_to_adf` before sending). Modelling the wire conversion as its own operation is what makes
the Protocol describe the real seam instead of a guess.

**Where each implementation lives — this is load-bearing, not a detail.**

- `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py` (new) holds the **Protocol** and `WikiTextCodec`. It imports nothing from
  `adapters/jira/`.
- `AdfCodec` lives in **`adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py`** (new, Cloud-side), NOT in `jira_family/`. It wraps
  the location-pinned `adapters/jira/adf.py`, and J2's machine-checked import contract forbids `jira_family/`
  from importing any Cloud vendor module — putting `AdfCodec` in `jira_family/` would fail that test. This is
  the same shape J2 already established: the shared layer defines the contract, the concrete adapter
  constructs the vendor-bound implementation.

The shared `map_fields_to_remote` then takes the codec as a constructor dependency, so exactly one
implementation of the mapping exists and the ADF-vs-wiki difference is a parameter. Cloud is constructed with
`AdfCodec` and its behavior is unchanged, proven by J1's pinned oracles [rebar:acb2-1823-2f0d-415b].

**`WikiTextCodec`'s limit and marker are specified here so the implementer does not invent them.**
`WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT = 32767` — Jira Server/DC's text-field cap, the same documented 32,767-character limit
`comment_limits._JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` already uses for comment bodies in this codebase. The truncation
marker is `" … [truncated by reconciler]"`, reusing `adf._ADF_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX`'s exact wording so a Jira
reader sees one consistent marker regardless of deployment. Both are module-level named constants with a
sourced comment, and the marker is counted against the limit so the fitted value never exceeds the cap
(matching `truncate_comment_body`'s existing rule). J5 [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7]'s live harness is where a
wrong limit would surface; if the live DC instance rejects at a different threshold, the constant moves and
this story's tests move with it.

**Out of scope: the inbound path and the location-pinned modules.** `inbound_fields.py`, `inbound_differ.py`
and the pinned `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` each carry their own `_load_adf()` lazy loader and their own
direct ADF calls. They are NOT re-pointed at the codec here: `outbound_fields.py` is location-pinned (ADR 0035
§(a)) and the inbound path is a separate seam with no DC caller yet. This story does not reduce their count of
ADF references, and its acceptance criteria are written to match that reality rather than to assert a
tree-wide absence that the story does not deliver.

**Back-out path.** The story lands as a single Gerrit change and is revertable with one `git revert`: it adds
two new modules and changes constructor wiring, touching no persisted data or store schema. The interface
change is delivered **expand-then-contract within the single change** — the codec is added and every Cloud
call site is re-pointed at it in the same commit, so no caller is ever left half-migrated and there is no
window in which two rich-text paths disagree.

**Alternative rejected:** a boolean or enum flag (`use_adf=True`) threaded through the mapper. It puts the
branch back inside the shared code, grows a branch per deployment type, and gives the codec no place to own its
own limit constant.

**Alternative rejected:** copying `map_fields_to_remote` per adapter (PR #120). One line differs; the other
thirty drift.

**Alternative rejected:** a two-operation Protocol (`fit_outbound` + `decode_inbound`) as originally sketched.
It cannot express the fit-vs-fit+normalize distinction the two existing Cloud callers rely on, so it would
force a silent behavior change on one of them.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py` (new) — the `RichTextCodec` Protocol
  and `WikiTextCodec`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py` (new) — `AdfCodec`, wrapping the
  location-pinned `adf.py` with no logic change.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/backend.py` — `_fit_description` re-expressed as
  `codec.normalize_outbound(codec.fit_outbound(v))`; Cloud constructed with `AdfCodec`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` — the injected `fit` becomes
  `AdfCodec().fit_outbound` (same function, now reached through the contract).
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_rich_text_codec.py` (new).
- **Out of scope:** `adapters/jira/adf.py`'s own logic, `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` (location-pinned),
  and the inbound path (`inbound_fields.py`, `inbound_differ.py`).

## Testing

Unit tier for each codec (pure transforms) plus a contract test run against BOTH implementations, since the
point of the story is that they are interchangeable behind one Protocol.

- shared contract, parameterized over both codecs: a short string survives
  `decode_inbound(to_wire(normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(s))))` unchanged; an over-limit string is fitted to
  at most that codec's limit, and its decoded form is a prefix of the original plus the truncation marker.
- shared contract: `decode_inbound(None) == ""` for both codecs.
- Cloud-specific: `AdfCodec.fit_outbound` returns exactly what `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit` returns for the same
  input, and `AdfCodec.to_wire` returns exactly what `adf.text_to_adf` returns — asserted against J1's pinned
  values, so the codec is proven to be a pass-through and not a reimplementation.
- Cloud-specific: `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(v))` equals the pre-story `_fit_description(v)` for the same
  input, pinning that the composition order is preserved.
- DC-specific: `WikiTextCodec` truncates at `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT`, the result ends with the truncation
  marker, and the total length does not exceed the limit; `to_wire` and `decode_inbound` are identity on `str`.
- contrast case: a non-`str` value is passed through untouched by both codecs rather than coerced, matching the
  current mapper's behavior; and a string already within the limit is returned unchanged (no marker appended).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] one parameterized contract test runs against both `AdfCodec` and `WikiTextCodec` and passes for each,
      covering all four operations
- [ ] `AdfCodec` output for the J1-pinned input equals the J1-pinned expected value for both `fit_outbound` and
      `to_wire`, and `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(v))` equals the pre-story `_fit_description(v)`
- [ ] **no NEW ADF reference is introduced outside the codec.** Verified by an allowlist, not a bare grep:
      `grep -rn '_load_adf\|fit_text_to_adf_limit' src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` returns hits ONLY in
      (a) `adapters/jira/adf.py` — the definitions; (b) `adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py` — `AdfCodec`;
      (c) `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py` — location-pinned, explicitly out of scope; (d) `inbound_fields.py`
      and `inbound_differ.py` — the inbound seam, explicitly out of scope. In particular there are **zero**
      hits under `adapters/jira_family/` or `adapters/jira_datacenter/`, and `backend.py` and `jira_fields.py`
      no longer reference either name directly (they go through the codec). A test encodes this allowlist so it
      is enforced rather than eyeballed
- [ ] `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py` imports nothing from `adapters/jira/` — J2's existing import-contract
      test must still pass, which it will only if `AdfCodec` lives on the Cloud side as specified
- [ ] exactly one definition of `map_fields_to_remote` exists in the tree
- [ ] `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` and the truncation marker exist as named module constants with a sourced
      comment, and a test pins that a fitted over-limit value ends with the marker and does not exceed the limit
- [ ] `decode_inbound(None)` returns `""` for both codecs, and a non-`str` value passes through both codecs
      untouched rather than being coerced
- [ ] J1's pinned Cloud oracles pass with their assertions unmodified
